acceptance.description: The approved acceptance manifest the feature was initialised with, by its SHA-256.

acceptance_review.description: The independent acceptance review between the last product node and the candidate: its policy, fixed at feature init, the review in flight and every settled one.

max_rounds.description: The budget per criterion: accepted reworks a materially new gap gets on its newness alone.

criterion_ceiling.description: The emergency ceiling of accepted reworks per criterion: past max_rounds each needs verified producer progress, and here a person decides.

reviewer_timeout_ms.description: How long a launched reviewer may run, from its launch, before it is interrupted and its generation re-issued.

refinement.description: A refinement of a settled review a valid challenge asked for: the challenges it decides, its round, the receipt and inputs of the review it refines.

coverage_sha256.description: The coverage manifest its receipt pins: every standing completion at its exact heads.

barrier.description: A PASS: the orchestration epoch it was settled at, no dispatch lease outstanding, every judged node DONE.

revision.description: The revision of the review this refinement made.

orders.description: What the revision did to each producer order of the review (engine/review-revision.ts).

revision.description: The review's current revision: 0 its original receipt, n after its n-th refinement.

criteria.description: The criteria that exhausted their own accepted-rework budget.

lineage.description: The per-criterion gap lineage (engine/review-lineage.ts): an append-only chain of what each criterion's gaps came to, each event bound by its hash to the one before. Budgets are summarized from it, never stored.

max_criterion_reworks.description: The budget per criterion: accepted reworks a materially new gap gets on its newness alone; past it, each one needs verified producer progress.

criterion_ceiling.description: The emergency ceiling per criterion, where a person decides (absent: the default).

max_review_ms.description: A configured review wall-clock budget, from the first review counted.

challenges.description: Review-gap challenges: a GAP whose exact public reproduction passed on the unchanged integrated head, oldest first.

partial.description: A per-criterion answer's challenge: the order's criteria it proved DONE in the same execution, and those it left unresolved.

evidence_repairs.description: Every stale evidence pointer the controller repaired from an exact archive (engine/evidence-integrity.ts), each bound by its receipt's hash.

evidence_repair.description: A delivery refused for evidence no exact archive restores (engine/evidence-integrity.ts): administrative, never a product rework; delivery fails closed until the controller repairs it.

orchestration.description: The orchestration epoch and the dispatch lease registry (state/orchestration.ts): the epoch moves in the same write as each change of what a review or a candidate binds; every claim and review generation is a lease from its issue to its close.

provider.description: Model-provider failures of lease holders: each interruption, the counts per ticket and per phase that bound them, and the stop past them.

testIdentity.description: A test's runner-aware canonical identity (evidence/test-identity.ts): its normalised source path and its runner's key (JUnit: the method, package and class stripped; JS and exact runners: the full name).

testIdentityAlias.description: A test published before canonical identities, mapped to its identity at a head, with the immutable receipt settle wrote of it.

partialOrder.description: The order a per-criterion answer settled, as its brief bound it.

hostSession.description: The host session a dispatch was handed to, as the plugin's fence saw it run dispatch: what a provider failure of that host is read from.

providerMark.description: A transient model-provider failure that ended a lease's holder, as Claude Code recorded it: class, sanitized request id and category, where it was read. Never a prompt or a reply.

agentInterruptMark.description: A launched reviewer interrupted before it completed: past its wall-clock, its host session's process gone, its task ended otherwise, or its launch failed. Its Agent call, its agent by hash, when it was launched and how long it ran. Never a prompt or an answer.

revision.description: The revision of the review the order is bound to.

restoration.description: An order restoring completed proofs the reviewed heads lost: never an accepted rework of their criteria.

revisionRef.description: A revision of an acceptance review: 0 its original receipt, n its n-th refinement's, pinned by its SHA-256.

reworkRebase.description: A review rework's order rebased from one revision of its review to a later one, each of its gaps carried unchanged; bound by its own SHA-256.

provider_interrupted.description: The generation's holder was ended by a transient model-provider failure after the worker made progress: the claim is kept for the same generation to resume, its old capability rotated away.

challenge_conversion.description: A review rework's legacy BLOCKED answer whose red gate passed every declared test, converted once into a request for the structured challenge: no attempt charged.

capsule_id.description: The claim's passing reproduction capsule that is the challenge's material, when there is one.

capsules.description: The reproduction capsules the claim's capability holder sealed (engine/reproduction-capsule.ts): each one's id, receipt and the receipt's hash. Only a capsule this registry holds is used by the claim.

review_rebase.description: The claim's order was rebased to a later revision of its review while it was held: its old capability rotated away, dispatch reissues the same generation from where it stands; no attempt charged.

identity_version.description: The canonical test identity version the refusal was judged under; absent before canonical identities.

identity_reconcile.description: The claim's answer re-evaluated administratively for an identity-shape refusal: bound to its exact controller copy; nothing charged.

challenge_red.description: The last red gate of an acceptance review rework whose declared tests all passed on the unchanged base.

accepted.description: The red gate accepted the RED (a declared test failed for a missing behaviour); the passing declared tests are what a per-criterion challenge cites.

challenge_reds.description: Every red gate of an acceptance review rework, on this claim, with a declared test that passed (accepted REDs among them): what a per-criterion challenge cites.

criteria_judged.description: The sealed head this claim's criterion evidence was judged and accepted at.

revalidation.description: The completed criteria this generation relies on, revalidated on the claim's base before any worker ran.

criteria_settlement.description: A per-criterion answer judged and on its way to DONE: what each ordered criterion came to.

reproof_unit.description: The re-proof unit settle committed on the sealed head (engine/proof-units.ts), journaled before the node branch moves to it.

lineage.description: The orchestration epoch the node's own generation last changed at (reworked, reopened, restored, invalidated).

restore_dependents.description: An acceptance review rework: each DONE product dependent it reopened, whole, for a valid challenge of the rework to restore with the node.

restore.description: An acceptance review rework: the DONE generation it replaced, whole, for a valid challenge to restore.

partial.description: A per-criterion answer settled this order: what each criterion came to (done, challenged, unresolved) and the unresolved criteria's own order.

superseded.description: A later revision of its review changed this order's gaps: replaced by a new order (amend) or withdrawn (cancel); it counts for nothing.

challenge_id.description: A criterion a per-criterion answer challenged: its prior proof, carried while the challenge waits.

capsule.description: A RED promoted from a failing reproduction capsule: the capsule whose files were committed test-first and failed again by the red gate.

reproof.description: An ordered criterion completed before: the review's reproduction shown passing on the unchanged base by a red gate of the claim.

ordered.description: The order names this completed criterion again: its completed proof, re-provable.

criterion_ledger.description: Every criterion the node completed by an accepted settlement (engine/criterion-ledger.ts).

compatibility_units.description: Compatibility-regression units: tests alone proving existing behaviour, apart from the RED cycles.

sibling_progress.description: Why settle last refused, uncharged, to integrate work that would lose a sibling's standing proof.

reopenedCriterion.description: A completed criterion the claim's base no longer holds as completed: ordered by this generation's own proof now, never charged.

criterionCompletion.description: A criterion completed by an accepted settlement: immutable, bound by sha256 (engine/criterion-ledger.ts).

commit.description: The re-proof unit settle committed it in (absent in a record from before re-proof units: never committed).
